info.title: flatin.pt API
info.summary: Portuguese home buying, machine-readable: new-build developments, where-to-live guides, municipality data, IMT and stamp duty (Imposto do Selo) on a purchase, IMI rates for all 308 municipalities.
info.description: Keyless public API of flatin.pt. Numbers are the same as on the site and come from the official tables; every successful JSON answer carries an attribution field — show it next to the numbers. Rate limits: 120 requests per minute per IP address, HTTP 429 with Retry-After when exceeded. Status: https://flatin.pt/status/. MCP server: https://flatin.pt/mcp.

get.summary: IMI rates for all municipalities
get.description: The yearly urban IMI rate of every Portuguese municipality for the latest verified tax year, or for `year` if given. Where a municipality sets no single rate (it is set per parish), the rate comes with `available: false` and the reason, never as zero. Every answer carries an `attribution` field.

get.summary: The same rates as one CSV file
get.description: Open data: the same rows as the JSON list, under the same licence (see the Link header). An empty rate cell means the municipality sets no single rate, not zero. `year` selects a verified past table.

get.summary: IMI rates with municipality boundaries (GeoJSON)
get.description: Open data for GIS: a GeoJSON FeatureCollection (WGS 84) with one polygon per municipality and flat properties `codigo`, `municipality`, `distrito`, `year`, `urban_available`, `urban_rate_percent` (a number, 0.3 means 0.3 %), `urban_reason`, `rural_rate_percent` and `page`. Where a municipality sets no single rate the rate is null, `urban_available` is false and `urban_reason` says why; never zero. Boundaries: CAOP (Direção-Geral do Território), simplified, CC BY 4.0, credit in the `boundaries` member. `year` selects a verified past table.

get.summary: Every verified year of IMI rates in one CSV file
get.description: Open data: one row per municipality per verified tax year (long format), columns `codigo`, `municipality`, `municipality_as_published`, `distrito`, `year`, `urban_rate_percent`, `rural_rate_percent` (numbers, 0.3 means 0.3 %) and `verified_on` (the date the year was checked against the source). An empty rate cell means the municipality sets no single rate, not zero. CC BY 4.0.

get.summary: IMI rate of one municipality
get.description: One municipality by its four-digit code or name, with the rate `history` by tax year and its `movement` (raised, lowered, unchanged, returned, not_comparable). An unknown municipality gets 404 with a link to the full list.

schema.description: Four-digit municipality code (1312) or its name (Porto)

post.summary: What a purchase costs on top of the price
post.description: IMT (property transfer tax), Imposto do Selo (stamp duty) and the property registration. Body: `value` (the contract price in euros), optional `territory` (`continente` or `regioes_autonomas`), `primary_home` (default true) and `buyer_is_young` (default false: 35 or under, first own permanent home, not an IRS dependant, no residential property owned in the previous three years), `non_resident` (default false: true for a buyer who is not and has never been tax resident in Portugal), `tax_haven_company` (default false: true when the buyer is a company or other entity with its tax domicile in a jurisdiction on the Portuguese list of more favourable tax regimes, or controlled by one; never an individual), and `vpt` (the valor patrimonial tributário from the caderneta predial, in euros; optional). A non-resident buyer pays IMT at a flat rate with no exemption or reduction (CIMT art. 17.º n.º 10): `imt_regime` is `non_resident_flat` instead of `tables`, the young buyers' table and the stamp duty deduction do not apply, and `annullable` gives what the Tax Authority annuls on request if the buyer becomes tax resident within the window or lets the home at a moderate rent (n.º 11–12) — two amounts, the months of each window and the request deadline. For a resident buyer `annullable` is null. A listed-regime company pays 10 % with no exemption or reduction (CIMT art. 17.º n.º 4), even when it is resident and even with `non_resident`: `imt_regime` is `tax_haven_flat` and `annullable` is null. IMT and stamp duty are charged on the higher of the contract price and the VPT (CIMT art. 12.º n.º 1; Código do Imposto do Selo art. 9.º n.º 4): `taxable_value_cents` is that base and `taxable_base` says which one it is (`price` or `vpt`). Without `vpt` the base is the price, and a higher VPT would make both taxes higher. `notary_estimate_cents` is the published price of one registration act at the Casa Pronta counter of the Ministério da Justiça. It does not cover the purchase contract at a notary, buying with a mortgage (a second registration act plus stamp duty on the loan) or the agency's fee — see `notes`. Annual IMI is not part of `total_cents`: it is charged on the VPT, not on the price — see /api/v1/imi/rates/{codigo} for the rate. For a young buyer the reduced IMT table applies and stamp duty is reduced by the deduction of art. 7.º-A of the Código do Imposto do Selo: `stamp_duty_cents` is the amount due, `stamp_duty_relief_cents` the deduction. Invalid input gets 422 with `error` and `field`.

get.summary: Building-permit barometer: monthly case counts per municipality
get.description: Open data (CC BY 4.0). One row per municipality, period and measure. `cases` counts municipal building-works cases entering the licensing pipeline, dated by that municipality's declared reference event — not licences granted, and not dwellings. `measure` follows the INE breakdown: new_build, alter_extend, total_works, plus unclassified (cases whose works type the municipality does not state) and pip (preliminary enquiries, counted apart). `provisional` marks periods the source layer is still back-filling. `vintage` is the day the series was snapshotted: pass it back to reproduce a citation. Every row carries the source layer it was counted from.

get.summary: The same barometer series as JSON, with attribution
get.description: The same rows as the CSV, plus an `attribution` object naming both data sources separately: our own counts from municipal GIS layers, and the official INE series used as context and as the population denominator.

get.summary: The official INE series the barometer is checked against
get.description: Open data (CC BY 4.0, source INE). Licensed buildings and dwellings per municipality, and resident population, exactly as INE publishes them — no processing of ours beyond reshaping. Each row carries the exact INE API call it came from and the date INE last updated that indicator. Note on municipality_code: it is DICOFRE on the mainland, but for the thirty municipalities of the Azores and Madeira it is the tax authority's own code (Funchal is 2203, not 3103), because that is the key the rest of this site uses. municipality_as_ine_publishes_it carries INE's own name for the row.

get.summary: ADENE energy-certificate statistics (SCE) for new housing
get.description: Mirror of ADENE's public SCE statistics, per month and municipality, for two measures: precert_new_housing (context 'Projeto Edifícios Novos', type 'Habitação') and completed_new_housing (context 'Edifícios Concluídos Novos', type 'Habitação'). Source: ADENE — SCE; credit it as such. A pre-certificate is issued for every dwelling at the DESIGN stage: it is not a building licence and not a construction start, and this series is not comparable one-to-one with INE's licensed dwellings. certificates is the sum over energy classes; avg_useful_area_m2 is the certificate-weighted mean of ADENE's per-class averages. A municipality with no row in a month had zero certificates that month (ADENE prints only non-zero rows). Coverage: mainland Portugal and Madeira. Note on municipality_code: DICOFRE on the mainland, but for Madeira it is the tax authority's code (Funchal is 2203, not 3103), the same key as the rest of this site. Each row carries the ADENE file it came from, that file's sha256 and the day we fetched it.

get.summary: Search new-build projects in Portugal
get.description: Published new-build projects (empreendimentos) with filters: municipality (Portuguese name, slug or four-digit code), parish, typology (T0–T5, repeatable; T5 means five bedrooms or more), price_min and price_max in euros, stage (planned, licensed, building, selling, delivered), delivery_by (year; completed or promised for that year or earlier, overdue promises included), energy_class (A+…F, repeatable), on_sale, sort (price, name, delivery, new), limit (1–50, default 10) and offset. language (pt, en, ru, ua, de, fr, nl) picks the language of page URLs and labels. Every result carries its canonical page URL; catalog_url is the same selection on the site.

400.description: A parameter is not valid: error, field, message

get.summary: One new-build project: prices, status, purchase cost, nearby
get.description: One published project by slug (or its page URL): prices and units per typology, price history, construction stage and delivery promises, linked building permits, the developer, the full purchase cost at the cheapest available price (IMT, stamp duty, registration; primary_home and buyer_is_young adjust it), nearby transport, schools, health, shops and parks, and the canonical page URL in each of the seven languages.

get.summary: Where to live in Portugal: the city guides compared, as CSV
get.description: Open data (CC BY 4.0, see the Link header): one row per flatin.pt 'where to live' city guide. IMI urban rate (min and max over the guide's municipalities, Portal das Finanças table for imi_year); INE median sale price per m2 (latest fresh quarter, min and max); new-build supply in the flatin.pt catalogue (developments, units for sale, median asking price per m2 over units with a floor area, only from 5 such units up); counts of areas the guide rates good / depends / avoid and of places named for recent police operations (dated official source, at most 24 months old). An empty cell means we hold no number, not zero.

get.summary: Where to live in a city: verdict by area, noise and safety
get.description: The verdict of a flatin.pt guide by area — live (good to live), depends (depends on you) or avoid (we advise against) — with the reason as written on the site, who each area suits, and the sources of its numbers. Sections: noise in plain words (festivals, bars, aircraft under approach paths), safety as dated, sourced police operations (local reputation of a place, never a claim about its residents), prices, municipal housing, climate, transport. `city` is a guide name in any site language, its slug, or a municipality inside a guide (Gaia → Greater Porto). A profile keeps the areas that suit it plus every 'avoid' area.

post.summary: Send a request to a licensed real estate agency (two steps)
post.description: The same as the MCP tool `request_consultation`, with the same body. `mode`: `link` (default) returns the form link and the consent text; `prepare` checks the details (`name`, `phone` + `channel` or else `email`, `city` or `project`, `language`, optional `budget`, `typology`, `intent`, `message`, `client`) and returns a `summary`, the GDPR consent text in the person's language, its `consent_text_version` and a `confirmation_token` (valid 30 minutes, not before 5 seconds); nothing is sent. `submit` sends the request to a licensed agency: the same details plus `confirmation_token`, `consent: true` and `consent_text_version` — only after the person has read the consent text and explicitly agreed. Changed details, a missing consent or an outdated text version are refused. The answer to `submit` is the same whether the request is new, a repeat or merged into an open one. Refusals: 422 with `error`, `message` and `field` or `problems`; 429 with `Retry-After` (30 prepares and 10 submits an hour per address, 5 accepted requests an hour per address).

post.summary: Subscribe an email to new developments or construction
post.description: The same as the MCP tool `subscribe_digest`, with the same body: `email`, `what` (`new_developments`, daily, the default; or `construction`, newly licensed construction, weekly), `city`, `parish` (construction only), `typology`, `price_min`, `price_max`, `on_sale`, `language`. It only sends a confirmation email (double opt-in): nothing is active until the person clicks the link, within 7 days. The answer is the same for a new address, a subscribed one and a repeat. Refusals: 422 with `error` and `field`; 429 with `Retry-After` (10 an hour per address, shared with the site's forms).
